figures.name: Hammurabi
figures.blurb: Unified Mesopotamia under Babylon and published one of the first written law codes, a model of public, written justice for later societies.

figures.name: Hatshepsut
figures.blurb: One of Egypt's most successful pharaohs; her trade voyage to Punt and building boom proved a woman could wield full royal power.

figures.name: Akhenaten
figures.blurb: Replaced Egypt's many gods with worship of the sun disk Aten, one of history's earliest experiments with something close to monotheism.

figures.name: Nefertiti
figures.blurb: Queen beside Akhenaten who helped lead his religious revolution; her painted bust, found in 1912, made her an icon of ancient power.

influenceNote.akhenaten: Queen and partner in Akhenaten's Aten revolution

figures.name: Suppiluliuma I
figures.blurb: Built the Hittite kingdom into an empire rivaling Egypt; a plague carried home by his war captives later killed him and his heir.

figures.name: Tutankhamun
figures.blurb: Boy king who restored Egypt's old gods; his nearly intact tomb, opened in 1922, sparked the modern world's fascination with ancient Egypt.

influenceNote.akhenaten: Likely his son; restored the old gods Akhenaten had banished

figures.name: Ramesses II
figures.blurb: Reigned 66 years, fought the Hittites at Kadesh, then signed the oldest surviving peace treaty; his monuments defined the image of a pharaoh.

figures.name: Hattusili III
figures.blurb: Made peace with Ramesses II around 1259 BCE in the oldest surviving peace treaty, ending generations of war between two empires.

influenceNote.suppiluliuma_i: Grandson who seized the throne and held the empire Suppiluliuma built
influenceNote.ramesses_ii: Old rival from Kadesh; they sealed one of the earliest known peace treaties

figures.name: Moses
figures.blurb: In Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition, led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Law; the Ten Commandments shaped Western ethics.

figures.name: Puduhepa
figures.blurb: Hittite queen who co-sealed treaties and wrote to Ramesses II as an equal, one of the most powerful women of the Bronze Age.

influenceNote.hattusili_iii: Wife and co-ruler; her seal sat beside his on the treaty with Egypt

figures.name: Zoroaster
figures.blurb: Founded Zoroastrianism; its ideas of one good god, a cosmic battle of good and evil, and a final judgment influenced later faiths. Dates uncertain.

figures.name: King David
figures.blurb: Traditionally united the tribes of Israel with Jerusalem as capital; his royal line became the root of Jewish and Christian messianic hopes.

influenceNote.moses: Ruled a people bound by the covenant and law tradition credits to Moses

figures.name: Hiram I of Tyre
figures.blurb: King who made Tyre the leading Phoenician city and hub of a Mediterranean trading network; he sent cedar and craftsmen to build Solomon's Temple.

figures.name: King Solomon
figures.blurb: Traditionally built the First Temple, making Jerusalem the religious center of Israel; his name became a byword for wisdom.

influenceNote.king_david: Son and successor; inherited the kingdom David united
influenceNote.hiram_i: Phoenician ally who sent cedar and craftsmen to build his Temple

figures.name: Hazael of Damascus
figures.blurb: Aramean king who made Damascus the Levant's leading power; his Tel Dan victory stele holds the oldest accepted mention of the House of David outside the Bible.

figures.name: Shammuramat
figures.blurb: Assyrian queen who held rare power, possibly as regent in her young son's early reign; her memory grew into the legend of Semiramis, the warrior queen.

figures.name: Homer
figures.blurb: Traditional poet of the Iliad and Odyssey, founding works of Western literature that gave scattered Greek city-states a shared identity.

figures.name: Tiglath-Pileser III
figures.blurb: Rebuilt Assyria with a standing army, governors and mass deportations, creating a template of imperial rule copied by later empires.

figures.name: Piye
figures.blurb: Kushite king from Nubia who conquered Egypt and founded its 25th Dynasty, showing that African kingdoms south of Egypt could rule the Nile.

figures.name: Isaiah
figures.blurb: Prophet whose visions of one universal God and a coming age of peace became central texts for both Judaism and Christianity.

influenceNote.king_david: Foretold a just king from David's line, a shoot from the stump of Jesse

figures.name: Ashurbanipal
figures.blurb: Last great Assyrian king; his library at Nineveh preserved thousands of clay tablets, including the Epic of Gilgamesh, for modern discovery.

figures.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
figures.blurb: Rebuilt Babylon into the greatest city of its age and destroyed Jerusalem in 587 BCE; the exile he imposed reshaped Judaism.

figures.name: Sappho
figures.blurb: Lyric poet of Lesbos whose personal voice about love and longing influenced poetry for millennia; ancients called her the tenth Muse.

influenceNote.homer: Her lyric poems borrow Homeric language, myths and heroes

figures.name: Cyrus the Great
figures.blurb: Founded the Persian Empire, the largest yet seen, and let exiled peoples like the Jews return home, a model of tolerant imperial rule.

figures.name: Croesus
figures.blurb: Lydian king whose realm minted early pure gold and silver coins, spreading money as a tool of trade; his fall brought Persia to the Aegean.

figures.name: Laozi
figures.blurb: Traditional author of the Tao Te Ching and founder of Taoism, which teaches harmony with nature and deeply shaped Chinese culture.

figures.name: Pythagoras
figures.blurb: Taught that the universe is ruled by number; his school's work on mathematics and musical harmony shaped Greek and European science.

figures.name: Confucius
figures.blurb: Taught that ethics, family duty and good government go together; his ideas guided Chinese education and civil service for 2,000 years.

figures.name: Darius I
figures.blurb: Organized Persia into provinces linked by roads, a royal post and standard coins; his invasion of Greece was turned back at Marathon.

influenceNote.cyrus_the_great: Seized and reorganized the empire Cyrus had founded
influenceNote.zoroaster: His inscriptions praise Ahura Mazda, the god Zoroaster preached

figures.name: Mahavira
figures.blurb: Great teacher of Jainism, whose principle of nonviolence toward all living beings later inspired Gandhi's political movement.

figures.name: Xerxes I
figures.blurb: Led the massive invasion of Greece in 480 BCE; defeat at Salamis and Plataea gave the Greek city-states room to flourish.

influenceNote.darius_i: Son and successor; renewed his father's war on Greece

figures.name: Pericles
figures.blurb: Led Athens in its golden age, funding the Parthenon and deepening democracy; rivalry with Sparta helped spark the Peloponnesian War.

figures.name: Herodotus
figures.blurb: Called the father of history; his inquiry into the causes of the Persian Wars created the idea of researching and explaining the past.

influenceNote.homer: Told the Persian Wars with an epic sweep modeled on Homer

figures.name: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
figures.blurb: Taught a path to end suffering through wisdom and compassion; Buddhism spread across Asia and now has hundreds of millions of followers.

figures.name: Socrates
figures.blurb: Taught by asking questions, founding Western ethics and critical thinking; his execution by Athens made him a martyr for free inquiry.

figures.name: Hippocrates
figures.blurb: Father of medicine who treated disease as natural rather than divine punishment; the Hippocratic Oath still guides doctors' ethics.

figures.name: Democritus
figures.blurb: Proposed that everything is made of tiny indivisible atoms moving through empty space, an idea physics confirmed 2,300 years later.

figures.name: Plato
figures.blurb: Student of Socrates who founded the Academy; his dialogues on justice, knowledge and ideal forms set the agenda of Western philosophy.

influenceNote.socrates: Student who made Socrates the voice of his dialogues
influenceNote.pythagoras: Took up Pythagorean ideas of number, harmony and the immortal soul

figures.name: Aristotle
figures.blurb: Tutor of Alexander who organized knowledge into logic, biology, ethics and politics; his system dominated science for nearly 2,000 years.

influenceNote.plato: Studied 20 years in Plato's Academy, then broke with his theory of Forms

figures.name: Alexander the Great
figures.blurb: Conquered from Greece to India in about a decade, spreading Greek language and ideas across Asia and opening the Hellenistic age.

influenceNote.homer: Slept with the Iliad under his pillow and modeled himself on Achilles
influenceNote.cyrus_the_great: Admired Cyrus and had his looted tomb at Pasargadae restored

figures.name: Chandragupta Maurya
figures.blurb: Founded the Maurya Empire after Alexander's retreat, the first state to unite most of the Indian subcontinent.

influenceNote.alexander_the_great: Rose in the power vacuum Alexander's retreat from India left

figures.name: Euclid
figures.blurb: Assembled the Elements, the geometry textbook used for over 2,000 years, which taught generations to build knowledge by logical proof.

influenceNote.pythagoras: His Elements organized earlier Greek geometry, Pythagoras's theorem included

figures.name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus
figures.blurb: Expanded the Library and Museum of Alexandria into the ancient world's greatest research center, drawing scholars from everywhere.

influenceNote.alexander_the_great: Heir of Alexander's general Ptolemy; ruled from the city Alexander founded

figures.name: Ashoka
figures.blurb: Maurya emperor who renounced war after the bloody Kalinga campaign and sent Buddhist missions abroad, helping make Buddhism a world religion.

influenceNote.chandragupta_maurya: Grandson who inherited and expanded the Maurya Empire
influenceNote.buddha: After the carnage at Kalinga, embraced Buddhism and spread it across Asia

figures.name: Archimedes
figures.blurb: Mathematician and engineer of Syracuse who found the laws of the lever and buoyancy; his methods foreshadowed calculus.

influenceNote.euclid: Built his geometry on Euclid's Elements and the Alexandrian school
influenceNote.democritus: Credited Democritus as first to state the volume of a cone, though unproved

figures.name: Eratosthenes
figures.blurb: Head of the Library of Alexandria who measured Earth's circumference using shadows and geometry, remarkably close to the true value.

influenceNote.archimedes: Friend of Archimedes, who addressed his treatise The Method to him

figures.name: Qin Shi Huang
figures.blurb: First emperor to unify China in 221 BCE; he standardized writing, money and measures and linked the first Great Wall, creating the Chinese state.

figures.name: Hannibal Barca
figures.blurb: Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps with elephants and nearly broke Rome; his defeat left Rome master of the Mediterranean.

figures.name: Modu Chanyu
figures.blurb: Founded the Xiongnu steppe empire whose pressure on Han China drove wall building and the westward diplomacy that opened the Silk Road.

figures.name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
figures.blurb: Tried to force Greek religion on Judea, provoking the Maccabean revolt, whose victory is still remembered at Hanukkah.

figures.name: Menander I
figures.blurb: Indo-Greek king remembered in the Buddhist text Milinda's Questions, a symbol of the meeting of Greek and Indian thought.

influenceNote.buddha: Questioned Buddhist teaching with the monk Nagasena in the Milinda Panha

figures.name: Mithridates II of Parthia
figures.blurb: Expanded Parthia to its peak and exchanged envoys with Han China, helping establish the Silk Road trade across Asia.

figures.name: Emperor Wu of Han
figures.blurb: Made Confucianism state doctrine, expanded China and sent Zhang Qian west, opening the Silk Road to Central Asia and beyond.

influenceNote.confucius: Made Confucian teaching the official learning of the Han state
influenceNote.qin_shi_huang: Ruled the unified, centralized empire Qin Shi Huang had created

figures.name: Cicero
figures.blurb: Orator and statesman whose writings on law, duty and republics shaped Latin prose and later inspired America's founders.

influenceNote.plato: Modeled his Republic and Laws on Plato's dialogues

figures.name: Julius Caesar
figures.blurb: Conquered Gaul and seized power in Rome; his murder set off civil wars that turned the Republic into an Empire. His calendar, revised, is still ours.

influenceNote.alexander_the_great: Lamented before Alexander's statue at having done so little by the same age

figures.name: Cleopatra VII
figures.blurb: Last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt; her alliances with Caesar and Antony shaped Rome's civil wars, and her fall made Egypt a Roman province.

influenceNote.julius_caesar: Caesar's backing won her Egypt's throne; she bore his son Caesarion

figures.name: Augustus
figures.blurb: First Roman emperor, who ended civil war and began the Pax Romana, two centuries of stability in which roads, trade and Christianity spread.

influenceNote.julius_caesar: Great-nephew and adopted heir who built an empire on Caesar's legacy

figures.name: Arminius
figures.blurb: Germanic chief who destroyed three Roman legions in the Teutoburg Forest in 9 CE, keeping Rome out of Germany and shaping Europe's map.

influenceNote.augustus: Served in Augustus's army, then destroyed three of its legions in 9 CE

figures.name: Jesus of Nazareth
figures.blurb: Jewish teacher in Roman Judea whose crucifixion and reported resurrection founded Christianity, now the world's largest religion.

influenceNote.moses: A Jewish teacher who taught by interpreting the Law of Moses
influenceNote.isaiah: Read Isaiah's prophecy aloud as his mission statement (Luke 4)

figures.name: Paul the Apostle
figures.blurb: Spread Christianity to non-Jews across the Roman world; his letters form much of the New Testament and shaped Christian theology.

influenceNote.jesus: Persecutor turned apostle who carried Jesus's message to non-Jews

figures.name: Ban Zhao
figures.blurb: China's first known female historian; she completed the Book of Han and wrote an influential guide to women's education.

influenceNote.confucius: Her Lessons for Women applied Confucian ethics to women's lives

figures.name: Cai Lun
figures.blurb: Han court official credited with perfecting papermaking around 105 CE; cheap paper later carried learning and printing worldwide.

figures.name: Claudius Ptolemy
figures.blurb: Alexandrian astronomer whose Earth-centered model of the cosmos was accepted for 1,400 years, until Copernicus and Galileo overturned it.

influenceNote.aristotle: Built his Earth-centered cosmos on Aristotle's physics

figures.name: Marcus Aurelius
figures.blurb: Philosopher-emperor whose private Stoic journal, the Meditations, is still read as a guide to self-discipline; his death ended the Pax Romana.

figures.name: Ardashir I
figures.blurb: Overthrew the Parthians and founded the Sasanian Empire, which revived Persian power and rivaled Rome for four centuries.

influenceNote.zoroaster: Founded the Sasanian dynasty as champion of the Zoroastrian faith

figures.name: Mani
figures.blurb: Prophet who founded Manichaeism, a faith blending Zoroastrian, Christian and Buddhist ideas that spread from Rome to China.

influenceNote.zoroaster: Claimed to complete the revelation Zoroaster brought to Persia
influenceNote.buddha: Claimed to complete the revelation the Buddha brought to India
influenceNote.jesus: Called himself an apostle of Jesus, completing his message

figures.name: Constantine the Great
figures.blurb: First Christian emperor; he legalized Christianity and founded Constantinople, which carried Roman rule for another thousand years.

influenceNote.jesus: First Christian emperor; legalized and funded the Church

figures.name: Augustine of Hippo
figures.blurb: Bishop and philosopher whose ideas on grace, sin and the City of God shaped Western Christianity and later the Reformation.

influenceNote.plato: Neoplatonism led him to a spiritual, non-material idea of God
influenceNote.paul_the_apostle: Converted in 386 after reading Paul's letter to the Romans
influenceNote.cicero: Cicero's lost Hortensius first turned him to philosophy
influenceNote.mani: Spent nine years as a Manichaean before rejecting it

figures.name: Hypatia
figures.blurb: Mathematician and philosopher who taught in Alexandria; her murder by a Christian mob became a lasting symbol of lost ancient learning.

influenceNote.plato: Taught Neoplatonist philosophy to students in Alexandria
influenceNote.claudius_ptolemy: Helped her father Theon edit and explain Ptolemy's Almagest

figures.name: Alaric I
figures.blurb: Visigothic king whose sack of Rome in 410, the first in 800 years, shocked the Roman world and inspired Augustine's City of God.

figures.name: Galla Placidia
figures.blurb: Ruled the Western Roman Empire as regent for her young son Valentinian III in 425-437, holding a fracturing empire together amid invasions.

influenceNote.alaric_i: Taken captive by Alaric's Goths around 410; later wed their king Ataulf

figures.name: Attila the Hun
figures.blurb: Leader of the Huns whose raids shook both halves of the Roman Empire, driving migrations that hastened the fall of the West.

figures.name: Odoacer
figures.blurb: Germanic general who deposed the last western emperor in 476, the date traditionally marking the fall of Rome and start of the Middle Ages.

figures.name: Clovis I
figures.blurb: United the Franks and converted to Catholic Christianity, creating the kingdom that became France and allying it with the Roman Church.

influenceNote.constantine_the_great: Gregory of Tours hailed his baptism as that of a new Constantine

figures.name: Aryabhata
figures.blurb: Mathematician-astronomer who used place-value numbers, approximated pi and argued that Earth spins, feeding Indian and Islamic science.

figures.name: Justinian I
figures.blurb: Byzantine emperor whose Code of Civil Law became the basis of many European legal systems; he also built the Hagia Sophia.

figures.name: Empress Theodora
figures.blurb: Byzantine empress and partner in power to Justinian who saved his throne in the Nika riots and pushed for laws protecting women.

influenceNote.justinian_i: Justinian had the law changed so he could marry her, a former actress

figures.name: Khosrow I
figures.blurb: Reformed taxes and welcomed exiled scholars to Persia, preserving Greek and Indian learning that later fed the Islamic golden age.

influenceNote.justinian_i: Welcomed Greek philosophers after Justinian shut the pagan schools

figures.name: Khadijah
figures.blurb: Successful merchant who married Muhammad and was the first to accept his message; her wealth and support sustained early Islam.

figures.name: Muhammad
figures.blurb: Prophet of Islam who united Arabia under one faith; within a century Islam spread from Spain to India, and it now has nearly 2 billion followers.

influenceNote.khadijah: First wife and first believer; her wealth and faith sustained his mission
influenceNote.moses: The Quran honors Moses as a prophet and retells his story
influenceNote.jesus: The Quran honors Jesus as a prophet and the messiah

figures.name: Prince Shotoku
figures.blurb: Regent who promoted Buddhism, Chinese-style government and a 17-article constitution, shaping the early Japanese state.

influenceNote.buddha: Championed Buddhism in Japan, founding temples such as Horyu-ji
influenceNote.confucius: His Seventeen-Article Constitution drew on Confucian ideals

figures.name: Brahmagupta
figures.blurb: First to write rules for computing with zero and negative numbers; his work passed through Baghdad to Europe as modern arithmetic.

influenceNote.aryabhata: Built on, and sharply criticized, Aryabhata's astronomy

figures.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
figures.blurb: Muhammad's cousin and fourth caliph; the dispute over his leadership split Islam into the Sunni and Shia branches that persist today.

influenceNote.muhammad: Cousin, son-in-law and early convert; Shia Muslims see him as heir

figures.name: Wu Zetian
figures.blurb: The only woman to rule China as emperor in her own name; she widened the exam-based civil service and promoted Buddhism.

influenceNote.buddha: Used Buddhism to legitimize the rule of China's only female emperor

figures.name: Liutprand
figures.blurb: Strongest of the Lombard kings of Italy; his 728 Donation of Sutri gave the Pope his first sovereign territory, the seed of the Papal States.

figures.name: Charles Martel
figures.blurb: Frankish leader who defeated an Umayyad army at Tours in 732, halting Muslim expansion into northern Europe and founding the Carolingian line.

influenceNote.clovis_i: Ran the Frankish kingdom Clovis founded as its mayor of the palace

figures.name: Charlemagne
figures.blurb: United most of Western Europe and was crowned emperor in 800; his revival of learning and law laid the foundations of medieval Europe.

influenceNote.charles_martel: Grandson who inherited the Frankish power Martel built
influenceNote.augustine_of_hippo: Einhard says Augustine's City of God was his favorite book

figures.name: Harun al-Rashid
figures.blurb: Abbasid caliph whose Baghdad was among the richest cities on Earth; his court's patronage fed the House of Wisdom and Arabian Nights legends.

figures.name: Al-Khwarizmi
figures.blurb: Baghdad scholar whose books gave us algebra and spread Hindu-Arabic numerals; the word algorithm comes from his name.

influenceNote.brahmagupta: His Sindhind star tables drew on Brahmagupta's astronomy in Arabic translation
influenceNote.claudius_ptolemy: His world geography revised Ptolemy's map coordinates

figures.name: Simeon I the Great
figures.blurb: Tsar who made Bulgaria the leading Balkan power and sponsored the literary schools where the Cyrillic alphabet took shape.

figures.name: Erik the Red
figures.blurb: Norse explorer who founded the first European settlements in Greenland around 985, a stepping stone toward North America.

figures.name: Ibn al-Haytham
figures.blurb: Pioneer of the experimental method whose Book of Optics explained vision and light; it later guided Europe's scientists and lens makers.

influenceNote.claudius_ptolemy: Wrote Doubts on Ptolemy and rebuilt optics on experiment
influenceNote.euclid: Overturned Euclid's idea that the eye sends out rays of sight

figures.name: Leif Erikson
figures.blurb: Norse explorer who reached North America around 1000 CE at a place called Vinland, about 500 years before Columbus.

influenceNote.erik_the_red: Son of Erik, who founded the Norse colony in Greenland

figures.name: Bi Sheng
figures.blurb: Invented movable-type printing with clay characters in the 1040s, four centuries before Gutenberg's press.

figures.name: Murasaki Shikibu
figures.blurb: Court lady who wrote The Tale of Genji around 1010, often called the world's first novel and a foundation of Japanese literature.

figures.name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
figures.blurb: Persian physician-philosopher whose Canon of Medicine was a standard medical textbook in Europe and the Islamic world for 600 years.

influenceNote.aristotle: Read Aristotle's Metaphysics 40 times and built his philosophy on it
influenceNote.hippocrates: His Canon of Medicine built on the Hippocratic tradition

figures.name: Cnut the Great
figures.blurb: Viking king who ruled England, Denmark and Norway as one North Sea empire, tying Scandinavia into Christian Europe.

figures.name: Harald Hardrada
figures.blurb: Norwegian king whose 1066 invasion of England failed at Stamford Bridge, weakening the English army just before the Norman conquest.

figures.name: William the Conqueror
figures.blurb: Duke of Normandy who conquered England in 1066, blending French into the English language and centralizing English government.

influenceNote.harald_hardrada: Hardrada's invasion pulled Harold north days before William landed

figures.name: Pope Urban II
figures.blurb: Pope who launched the First Crusade in 1095, starting two centuries of holy wars between Christian Europe and the Muslim world.

influenceNote.charlemagne: One account of his Clermont crusade speech urges knights to follow Charlemagne

figures.name: Hildegard of Bingen
figures.blurb: Abbess, composer and naturalist whose music, visions and medical writings made her one of the most influential women of the Middle Ages.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
figures.blurb: Andalusian philosopher whose commentaries on Aristotle revived Greek thought in Christian Europe, influencing Aquinas and the universities.

influenceNote.aristotle: Wrote so many Aristotle commentaries he was called The Commentator
influenceNote.avicenna: Criticized Avicenna's readings to recover a purer Aristotle

figures.name: Minamoto no Yoritomo
figures.blurb: Founded the Kamakura shogunate in 1192, beginning nearly 700 years of rule by military warriors in Japan.

figures.name: Genghis Khan
figures.blurb: United the Mongol tribes and built the largest contiguous land empire in history, linking East and West through conquest and trade.

figures.name: Fibonacci
figures.blurb: Italian mathematician whose Book of Calculation spread Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe, transforming commerce, banking and science.

influenceNote.al_khwarizmi: Liber Abaci spread the numerals and algebra of al-Khwarizmi's books

figures.name: Sorghaghtani Beki
figures.blurb: Mongol princess who steered her sons Mongke, Kublai and Hulagu to power and promoted religious tolerance and farming across the empire.

influenceNote.genghis_khan: Genghis married her to his son Tolui

figures.name: Kublai Khan
figures.blurb: Grandson of Genghis who conquered China and founded the Yuan dynasty, reuniting China and opening it to foreign travelers.

influenceNote.genghis_khan: Grandson who completed the conquest of China that Genghis began
influenceNote.sorghaghtani_beki: Mother who schooled him and taught tolerance of Chinese ways

figures.name: Hulagu Khan
figures.blurb: Destroyed Baghdad in 1258, ending the Abbasid caliphate and the greatest center of the Islamic golden age.

influenceNote.genghis_khan: Grandson who carried Mongol conquest west to Baghdad
influenceNote.sorghaghtani_beki: Mother who raised him and won the throne for her sons

figures.name: Thomas Aquinas
figures.blurb: Blended Aristotle's philosophy with Christian theology, arguing faith and reason can coexist and shaping Catholic thought ever since.

influenceNote.aristotle: Fused Aristotle's philosophy with Christian theology
influenceNote.augustine_of_hippo: Cited Augustine more than any other Church Father
influenceNote.averroes: Used and argued against Averroes' Aristotle commentaries
influenceNote.avicenna: His On Being and Essence builds on Avicenna's metaphysics

figures.name: Marco Polo
figures.blurb: Venetian merchant who served at Kublai Khan's court; his book of travels stirred European interest in Asia and later inspired Columbus.

influenceNote.kublai_khan: Served at Kublai's court for 17 years

figures.name: Osman I
figures.blurb: Founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299, the seed of an empire that lasted over 600 years.

figures.name: Dante Alighieri
figures.blurb: Wrote the Divine Comedy in Italian rather than Latin, helping create the Italian language and opening the way to Renaissance literature.

influenceNote.thomas_aquinas: Thomist theology shapes the Comedy; Aquinas speaks in its Paradiso
influenceNote.aristotle: Called Aristotle the master of those who know

figures.name: Catherine of Siena
figures.blurb: Mystic and activist who urged the Pope to return from Avignon to Rome in 1377, restoring the papacy's historic seat.

figures.name: Margaret I of Denmark
figures.blurb: Queen who united Denmark, Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union in 1397, one of the largest European realms of its day.

figures.name: Zheng He
figures.blurb: Ming admiral whose treasure fleets reached East Africa decades before Columbus; China's later retreat from the seas left the oceans to Europe.

figures.name: Johannes Gutenberg
figures.blurb: Built the movable-type printing press around 1440, making books cheap and fueling the Reformation, Renaissance and Scientific Revolution.

figures.name: Joan of Arc
figures.blurb: Peasant girl who led French troops to lift the siege of Orleans in 1429, turning the Hundred Years' War and inspiring French nationhood.

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.blurb: Conquered Constantinople in 1453 with giant cannons, ending the Byzantine Empire and pushing Greek scholars west to feed the Renaissance.

influenceNote.osman_i: Heir of Osman's dynasty who took Constantinople in 1453
influenceNote.alexander_the_great: Had Alexander's life read to him and aimed to rival him

figures.name: Ivan III
figures.blurb: Ended Mongol overlordship in 1480 and tripled Moscow's territory, founding the Russian state.

figures.name: Isabella I of Castile
figures.blurb: Queen who completed the conquest of Granada and funded Columbus's 1492 voyage, launching Spain's global empire.

figures.name: Christopher Columbus
figures.blurb: Genoese navigator sailing for Spain whose 1492 voyage linked the Americas to Europe, starting the Columbian Exchange that remade both worlds.

influenceNote.marco_polo: Carried and annotated a copy of Marco Polo's travels
influenceNote.claudius_ptolemy: Ptolemy's too-small Earth and too-wide Asia made sailing west look short

figures.name: Leonardo da Vinci
figures.blurb: Painter of the Mona Lisa and engineer-anatomist whose notebooks fused art and science, the model of the Renaissance genius.

figures.name: Guru Nanak
figures.blurb: Founded Sikhism, preaching one God and the equality of all people regardless of caste; Sikhism now has about 25 million followers.

figures.name: Niccolo Machiavelli
figures.blurb: Wrote The Prince, describing politics as it is rather than as it should be, and so founded modern political science.

figures.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
figures.blurb: Proposed that Earth orbits the Sun; his 1543 book launched the Scientific Revolution and moved humanity from the center of the cosmos.

influenceNote.claudius_ptolemy: Rebuilt Ptolemy's Almagest around a moving Earth
influenceNote.pythagoras: Cited Pythagorean thinkers who had already set the Earth in motion

figures.name: Michelangelo
figures.blurb: Sculptor of David and painter of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, whose works defined the High Renaissance and the idea of artistic genius.

influenceNote.dante: Revered Dante; his Last Judgment borrows Dante's boatman Charon

figures.name: Ferdinand Magellan
figures.blurb: Portuguese captain sailing for Spain whose expedition made the first voyage around the world, revealing the true size of the oceans.

influenceNote.columbus: Pursued the westward route to the Spice Islands Columbus had sought

figures.name: Martin Luther
figures.blurb: Challenged the Church with his 95 Theses in 1517; printing presses spread them fast, starting the Protestant Reformation and wars of religion.

influenceNote.augustine_of_hippo: An Augustinian friar whose theology of grace rested on Augustine
influenceNote.paul_the_apostle: Paul's letter to the Romans sparked his idea of faith alone
influenceNote.gutenberg: Printing presses spread his pamphlets across Europe in weeks

figures.name: Hernan Cortes
figures.blurb: Conquistador who toppled the Aztec Empire in 1521 with Indigenous allies and epidemic disease, beginning Spanish rule in Mexico.

influenceNote.columbus: Came to the Caribbean colonies Columbus founded, then invaded Mexico

figures.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
figures.blurb: Ottoman sultan at the empire's peak who besieged Vienna and reformed the law, earning the title Lawgiver.

influenceNote.mehmed_ii: Great-grandson who expanded the empire Mehmed made a world power

figures.name: Hurrem Sultan
figures.blurb: Enslaved captive who became Suleiman's wife and adviser, opening an era in which royal women shaped Ottoman politics.

influenceNote.suleiman: Enslaved in his harem, she became his wife and closest adviser

figures.name: John Calvin
figures.blurb: French reformer whose Calvinism spread to the Netherlands, Scotland and New England, shaping ideas of work, thrift and self-government.

influenceNote.martin_luther: Built his Reformed theology on Luther's break with Rome
influenceNote.augustine_of_hippo: Drew heavily on Augustine's teaching on grace and predestination

figures.name: Elizabeth I
figures.blurb: Queen whose 44-year reign saw the Spanish Armada defeated, Shakespeare's theater flourish and England's first colonies, launching British power.

figures.name: Oda Nobunaga
figures.blurb: Warlord who used massed firearms to begin unifying war-torn Japan, starting the end of the century-long Warring States era.

figures.name: Akbar the Great
figures.blurb: Mughal emperor who built a vast, efficient empire and promoted tolerance among Hindus, Muslims and others through debate and reform.

figures.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
figures.blurb: Founded the Tokugawa shogunate in 1603, bringing 250 years of peace and isolation that shaped Japan's distinct culture.

influenceNote.oda_nobunaga: Ally of Nobunaga, whose unification of Japan he completed
influenceNote.minamoto_no_yoritomo: Studied Yoritomo's history and revived his shogunate model

figures.name: Tycho Brahe
figures.blurb: Made the most accurate naked-eye planet observations ever; Kepler used his data to discover the laws of planetary motion.

influenceNote.copernicus: Admired Copernicus's math but built a hybrid Earth-centered model

figures.name: Miguel de Cervantes
figures.blurb: Wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel, which shaped the art of fiction and the Spanish language.

figures.name: Galileo Galilei
figures.blurb: Turned a telescope to the sky, found Jupiter's moons and backed a Sun-centered cosmos; his trial made him a symbol of science versus authority.

influenceNote.copernicus: His telescope discoveries defended Copernicus's Sun-centered system
influenceNote.archimedes: Called Archimedes divine and modeled his physics on him

figures.name: William Shakespeare
figures.blurb: Playwright whose 39 plays enriched the English language and storytelling worldwide; his works are performed more than any others.

influenceNote.cervantes: The lost play Cardenio, credited to him and Fletcher, drew on Don Quixote

figures.name: Johannes Kepler
figures.blurb: Used Tycho Brahe's data to show that planets move in ellipses, laws that Newton later explained with gravity.

influenceNote.tycho_brahe: Used Tycho's precise observations to discover elliptical orbits
influenceNote.copernicus: Defended Copernicus's Sun-centered system from his first book
influenceNote.pythagoras: His Harmony of the World sought Pythagorean music in the planets

figures.name: Rene Descartes
figures.blurb: Founded modern philosophy with I think, therefore I am, and joined algebra to geometry with coordinates, a key step toward calculus.

influenceNote.galileo: Shelved his treatise The World after Galileo's 1633 condemnation

figures.name: John Locke
figures.blurb: Argued people have natural rights to life, liberty and property and may replace unjust rulers, ideas at the core of the US Declaration.

influenceNote.descartes: Said reading Descartes first gave him a taste for philosophy

figures.name: Louis XIV
figures.blurb: The Sun King, who reigned 72 years and built Versailles, making France Europe's leading power and the model of absolute monarchy.

figures.name: Isaac Newton
figures.blurb: Discovered the laws of motion and universal gravitation and co-invented calculus, giving humanity a universe it could predict with math.

influenceNote.galileo: Built his laws of motion on Galileo's work on falling bodies
influenceNote.kepler: Explained Kepler's planetary laws with universal gravitation
influenceNote.descartes: Learned analytic geometry from Descartes, then refuted his vortex physics

figures.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
figures.blurb: Co-invented calculus with the notation we still use and described binary arithmetic, the number system inside every modern computer.

influenceNote.descartes: Built on and critiqued Descartes' philosophy and physics

figures.name: Peter the Great
figures.blurb: Modernized Russia along Western lines, built a navy and founded St. Petersburg, turning Russia into a European great power.

influenceNote.leibniz: Leibniz advised him on reforms and a Russian academy of sciences
influenceNote.louis_xiv: Modeled his palace at Peterhof on Louis's Versailles

figures.name: Voltaire
figures.blurb: Enlightenment writer who championed free speech, religious tolerance and reason, feeding the ideas behind the French Revolution.

influenceNote.john_locke: Championed Locke's empiricism and tolerance in his Letters on the English

figures.name: Benjamin Franklin
figures.blurb: Scientist whose electricity experiments and lightning rod made him famous; as a diplomat he won French support for American independence.

influenceNote.isaac_newton: His electrical experiments followed Newton's experimental method
influenceNote.socrates: His Autobiography credits the Socratic method for his style of argument

figures.name: Maria Theresa
figures.blurb: Habsburg ruler for 40 years who modernized Austria's army, taxes and schools, introducing compulsory primary education in 1774.

figures.name: Adam Smith
figures.blurb: His Wealth of Nations (1776) explained how markets, division of labor and self-interest create prosperity, founding modern economics.

influenceNote.isaac_newton: Hailed Newton's system as the model of a science built on simple laws

figures.name: Catherine the Great
figures.blurb: Expanded Russia to the Black Sea and championed Enlightenment arts and learning, making Russia a leading European power.

influenceNote.voltaire: Corresponded with Voltaire for 15 years and bought his library
influenceNote.peter_the_great: Continued Peter's Westernization and raised the Bronze Horseman to him

figures.name: George Washington
figures.blurb: Led the Continental Army to victory and served as first US president, setting the precedent of peacefully giving up power.

figures.name: James Watt
figures.blurb: Made the steam engine far more efficient with a separate condenser, powering factories and the Industrial Revolution; the watt is named for him.

figures.name: Thomas Jefferson
figures.blurb: Wrote the Declaration of Independence proclaiming that all men are created equal, and doubled the US with the Louisiana Purchase.

influenceNote.john_locke: Echoed Locke's natural rights in the Declaration of Independence
influenceNote.isaac_newton: Counted Newton among his trinity of the three greatest men
influenceNote.benjamin_franklin: Franklin edited his draft of the Declaration in 1776

figures.name: Antoine Lavoisier
figures.blurb: Father of modern chemistry who named oxygen and hydrogen and showed mass is conserved in reactions; he was guillotined in the Revolution.

figures.name: Alexander Hamilton
figures.blurb: First US Treasury Secretary, who built the nation's financial system, public credit and first national bank.

influenceNote.george_washington: Washington's wartime aide and his first Treasury secretary
influenceNote.adam_smith: His Report on Manufactures engaged Smith's Wealth of Nations

figures.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
figures.blurb: Rose from the Revolution to rule much of Europe; his wars spread nationalism and his Napoleonic Code still underlies many legal systems.

influenceNote.alexander_the_great: Idolized Alexander and followed him into Egypt
influenceNote.julius_caesar: Studied Caesar's campaigns and dictated a history of them on St Helena
influenceNote.charlemagne: Crowned emperor in 1804 claiming Charlemagne's mantle

figures.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
figures.blurb: Composed through deafness, bridging the Classical and Romantic eras; his Ninth Symphony's Ode to Joy is now Europe's anthem.

influenceNote.napoleon: Dedicated the Eroica to him, then tore it up when he became emperor

figures.name: Michael Faraday
figures.blurb: Discovered electromagnetic induction, the principle behind every electric generator and motor that powers the modern world.

figures.name: Charles Darwin
figures.blurb: Explained evolution by natural selection in 1859, showing all life shares common ancestors and that humans are one branch of life's tree.

figures.name: Abraham Lincoln
figures.blurb: Led the Union through the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation, preserving the nation and ending slavery in the US.

influenceNote.george_washington: Revered Washington from a boyhood reading of his biography
influenceNote.thomas_jefferson: Built his antislavery case on Jefferson's Declaration of Independence

figures.name: Otto von Bismarck
figures.blurb: Unified Germany in 1871 through three wars and created the first state social insurance, a model for modern welfare states.

figures.name: Ada Lovelace
figures.blurb: Published the first computer program, for Babbage's engine, and foresaw that computers could handle music and symbols, not just numbers.

figures.name: Frederick Douglass
figures.blurb: Escaped slavery and became the leading abolitionist voice; his speeches and autobiography exposed slavery's cruelty to the world.

figures.name: Karl Marx
figures.blurb: German thinker who wrote Das Kapital in London; his theory of class struggle inspired communist revolutions that ruled a third of humanity.

influenceNote.adam_smith: Built his critique of capitalism on Smith's labor theory of value
influenceNote.democritus: Wrote his doctoral thesis on the atomism of Democritus and Epicurus

figures.name: Queen Victoria
figures.blurb: Reigned 63 years as Britain's industrial empire grew to cover about a fifth of the world's land; her era gave its name to an age.

figures.name: Susan B. Anthony
figures.blurb: Campaigned for decades for women's suffrage, paving the way for the 19th Amendment that gave US women the vote in 1920.

influenceNote.frederick_douglass: Longtime ally from the abolition movement; they split over the 15th Amendment

figures.name: Gregor Mendel
figures.blurb: Monk whose pea-plant experiments revealed the laws of heredity; rediscovered in 1900, they became the foundation of genetics.

influenceNote.charles_darwin: Read and annotated Darwin's Origin of Species

figures.name: Louis Pasteur
figures.blurb: Proved that germs cause disease and spoilage, made vaccines for rabies and anthrax and invented pasteurization, saving countless lives.

figures.name: Harriet Tubman
figures.blurb: Escaped slavery, then returned about 13 times to lead some 70 people to freedom on the Underground Railroad and later scouted for the Union.

figures.name: Rani Lakshmibai
figures.blurb: Queen of Jhansi who fought British forces in the 1857 uprising, becoming a lasting symbol of Indian resistance to colonial rule.

figures.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
figures.blurb: Created the periodic table in 1869 and predicted undiscovered elements, organizing all of chemistry.

influenceNote.lavoisier: Built on Lavoisier's modern definition and list of chemical elements

figures.name: Empress Dowager Cixi
figures.blurb: Effectively ruled Qing China for nearly 50 years; her resistance to deep reform helped bring the empire's collapse in 1912.

figures.name: Thomas Edison
figures.blurb: Invented the phonograph, a practical light bulb and power stations, and created the industrial research lab, electrifying modern life.

influenceNote.michael_faraday: Read Faraday's Experimental Researches in Electricity as a young man

figures.name: Alexander Graham Bell
figures.blurb: Patented the telephone in 1876, beginning a revolution in instant personal communication.

figures.name: Emperor Meiji
figures.blurb: Presided over the Meiji Restoration, which turned feudal Japan into an industrial and military power within decades.

figures.name: Nikola Tesla
figures.blurb: Serbian-American inventor of the alternating-current motor and power system that runs today's electric grids.

influenceNote.thomas_edison: Worked for Edison, then fought his DC system with alternating current

figures.name: Sigmund Freud
figures.blurb: Founded psychoanalysis, arguing hidden desires drive behavior; his ideas transformed psychology, art and popular culture.

influenceNote.charles_darwin: Said Darwin's theories drew him toward a career in science

figures.name: Henry Ford
figures.blurb: Introduced the moving assembly line in 1913, making cars affordable to millions and spreading mass production worldwide.

influenceNote.thomas_edison: Chief engineer at an Edison company; Edison cheered on his gasoline car in 1896

figures.name: Sun Yat-sen
figures.blurb: Revolutionary leader who helped overthrow China's last dynasty in 1911-12 and is revered as the father of modern China.

influenceNote.abraham_lincoln: Likened his Three Principles to Lincoln's of, by and for the people

figures.name: Marie Curie
figures.blurb: Discovered polonium and radium and pioneered radioactivity research; first person to win two Nobel Prizes, she helped open the atomic age.

figures.name: Wilbur Wright
figures.blurb: With his brother Orville, made the first powered, controlled airplane flights in 1903, beginning the age of aviation.

figures.name: Mahatma Gandhi
figures.blurb: Led India to independence through mass nonviolent resistance, a method later adopted by Martin Luther King Jr. and movements worldwide.

influenceNote.jesus: Called the Sermon on the Mount a key source of his nonviolence
influenceNote.mahavira: Grew up amid Jain ideals of ahimsa, nonviolence toward all life

figures.name: Vladimir Lenin
figures.blurb: Led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 and founded the Soviet Union, the first communist state, which shaped the 20th century.

influenceNote.karl_marx: Turned Marx's theory into a program for a revolutionary party

figures.name: Winston Churchill
figures.blurb: Prime minister who rallied Britain to fight on against Nazi Germany in 1940, helping the Allies win World War II.

figures.name: Joseph Stalin
figures.blurb: Soviet dictator whose forced industrialization and purges cost millions of lives; his armies helped defeat Nazi Germany, then the Cold War began.

influenceNote.lenin: Lenin's successor, who hardened his one-party state into a dictatorship
influenceNote.karl_marx: Ruled in the name of Marxism and forced collectivization

figures.name: Lise Meitner
figures.blurb: Physicist who, with Otto Frisch, explained nuclear fission in 1938, the discovery that led to nuclear power and the atomic bomb.

figures.name: Albert Einstein
figures.blurb: His relativity linked space, time, mass and energy (E=mc2), reshaping cosmology and explaining nuclear energy; GPS satellites must correct for it.

influenceNote.isaac_newton: Kept Newton's portrait on his wall; relativity rebuilt his physics
influenceNote.michael_faraday: Kept Faraday's portrait on his wall; field ideas shaped relativity

figures.name: Alexander Fleming
figures.blurb: Discovered penicillin in 1928, the first antibiotic, which has since saved hundreds of millions of lives from bacterial infections.

figures.name: Pablo Picasso
figures.blurb: Spanish-born painter who co-founded Cubism in Paris, breaking single-viewpoint perspective and reshaping 20th-century art.

figures.name: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk
figures.blurb: Ottoman officer who founded the Republic of Turkey in 1923, replacing the sultanate with a secular, modernizing nation-state.

figures.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
figures.blurb: President who fought the Great Depression with the New Deal and led the US through World War II, building the modern American state.

figures.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
figures.blurb: First Lady turned diplomat who chaired the drafting of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the UN in 1948.

influenceNote.franklin_d_roosevelt: Wife and political partner; his presidency gave her a national voice

figures.name: Niels Bohr
figures.blurb: Explained the atom with quantum orbits and led the Copenhagen school that built quantum mechanics, the basis of modern electronics.

figures.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
figures.blurb: First prime minister of India, who built its democracy and science institutions and led the non-aligned movement.

influenceNote.mahatma_gandhi: Gandhi's protege, whom Gandhi named his political heir

figures.name: Adolf Hitler
figures.blurb: Nazi dictator who started World War II in Europe and organized the Holocaust; the war killed some 70 to 85 million people and remade the world.

figures.name: Edwin Hubble
figures.blurb: Proved that other galaxies lie beyond the Milky Way and that the universe is expanding, key evidence for the Big Bang.

figures.name: Charles de Gaulle
figures.blurb: Led the Free French in World War II and founded France's Fifth Republic, restoring French independence and influence.

influenceNote.winston_churchill: Churchill backed his Free French from London after France fell in 1940

figures.name: B. R. Ambedkar
figures.blurb: Born into an untouchable caste, he led the drafting of India's constitution, which outlawed untouchability and guaranteed equal rights.

influenceNote.buddha: Led a mass conversion of Dalits to Buddhism in 1956

figures.name: Francisco Franco
figures.blurb: Won the Spanish Civil War and ruled Spain as a dictator for 36 years; his death opened Spain's transition to democracy.

influenceNote.adolf_hitler: German planes and arms helped him win the Spanish Civil War

figures.name: Mao Zedong
figures.blurb: Founded the People's Republic of China in 1949; his Great Leap Forward famine and Cultural Revolution caused tens of millions of deaths.

influenceNote.karl_marx: Adapted Marxism to a peasant revolution in China
influenceNote.lenin: Built a Leninist party and state

figures.name: Amelia Earhart
figures.blurb: First woman to fly solo across the Atlantic, whose record flights and disappearance inspired generations of women in aviation.

figures.name: Hirohito (Emperor Showa)
figures.blurb: Emperor during Japan's militarist expansion and World War II; his 1945 surrender broadcast ended the war in the Pacific.

influenceNote.emperor_meiji: Grandson who reigned under the Meiji constitution

figures.name: Deng Xiaoping
figures.blurb: Opened China's economy to markets after 1978, lifting hundreds of millions out of poverty and making China an industrial giant.

influenceNote.mao_zedong: Veteran of Mao's revolution who later reversed his economics

figures.name: J. Robert Oppenheimer
figures.blurb: Led the Manhattan Project lab that built the first atomic bombs in 1945, beginning the nuclear age and its arms race.

influenceNote.niels_bohr: Revered Bohr, who advised the Los Alamos bomb project
influenceNote.albert_einstein: Einstein's 1939 letter to FDR set in motion the bomb project he led

figures.name: Grace Hopper
figures.blurb: Computer pioneer who built one of the first compilers, letting programmers write in words instead of machine code, which led to COBOL.

figures.name: Rachel Carson
figures.blurb: Her book Silent Spring (1962) exposed the harm of pesticides like DDT and launched the modern environmental movement.

figures.name: Simone de Beauvoir
figures.blurb: Wrote The Second Sex (1949), arguing that women are made, not born, into inferior roles, a founding text of modern feminism.

figures.name: Ronald Reagan
figures.blurb: President whose tax cuts, deregulation and Cold War pressure reshaped US politics and helped bring the Cold War to an end.

influenceNote.franklin_d_roosevelt: Voted for FDR four times and admired his fireside radio talks

figures.name: Alan Turing
figures.blurb: Defined the theory of computation, helped break Nazi Enigma codes, and asked whether machines can think, the question behind AI.

influenceNote.ada_lovelace: His 1950 paper answered Lady Lovelace's objection to thinking machines

figures.name: Rosa Parks
figures.blurb: Refused to give up her bus seat in 1955, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott and energizing the civil rights movement.

figures.name: Norman Borlaug
figures.blurb: Bred high-yield wheat that launched the Green Revolution, credited with saving hundreds of millions of people from famine.

figures.name: Jonas Salk
figures.blurb: Developed the first effective polio vaccine in 1955 and did not patent it, helping drive polio to the brink of eradication.

figures.name: Indira Gandhi
figures.blurb: India's first woman prime minister; she backed the Green Revolution and won the 1971 war, but also imposed emergency rule in 1975-77.

influenceNote.jawaharlal_nehru: Daughter and political heir of Nehru
influenceNote.mahatma_gandhi: Grew up inside Gandhi's independence movement

figures.name: John F. Kennedy
figures.blurb: President who steered through the Cuban Missile Crisis and set the goal of landing on the Moon; his assassination shocked the world.

influenceNote.winston_churchill: Admired Churchill; his thesis Why England Slept studied appeasement

figures.name: Katherine Johnson
figures.blurb: NASA mathematician whose orbital calculations helped send John Glenn into orbit and Apollo 11 to the Moon.

figures.name: Rosalind Franklin
figures.blurb: Her X-ray images of DNA, including Photo 51, were key evidence for its double helix structure, opening the way to modern genetics and biotechnology.

figures.name: Betty Friedan
figures.blurb: Her 1963 book The Feminine Mystique voiced the frustration of American housewives and sparked second-wave feminism; she co-founded NOW in 1966.

influenceNote.simone_de_beauvoir: Credited The Second Sex with shaping her own feminist thinking

figures.name: Malcolm X
figures.blurb: Powerful voice for Black pride and self-determination whose ideas shaped the Black Power movement.

influenceNote.muhammad: Became a Muslim; his 1964 hajj to Mecca reshaped his views on race

figures.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
figures.blurb: Led the civil rights movement with nonviolent protest, winning laws that ended legal segregation in the US; his dream speech echoes worldwide.

influenceNote.mahatma_gandhi: Adopted Gandhi's nonviolent resistance; visited India in 1959
influenceNote.jesus: A Baptist minister who grounded his activism in Jesus's ethic of love
influenceNote.rosa_parks: Her arrest launched the Montgomery bus boycott he led
influenceNote.augustine_of_hippo: Quoted Augustine, an unjust law is no law at all, in his Birmingham letter
influenceNote.abraham_lincoln: Gave his I Have a Dream speech at the Lincoln Memorial, invoking Lincoln

figures.name: Tu Youyou
figures.blurb: Found the malaria drug artemisinin in a traditional herbal remedy; it has saved millions of lives and won her the 2015 Nobel Prize.

influenceNote.mao_zedong: Found artemisinin in Project 523, a malaria program Mao approved in 1967

figures.name: Neil Armstrong
figures.blurb: First person to walk on the Moon, on July 20, 1969, the high point of the space race and a new view of Earth.

influenceNote.wilbur_wright: Carried a piece of the Wright Flyer to the Moon
influenceNote.john_f_kennedy: Kennedy's 1961 Moon challenge put him on the Moon in 1969

figures.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
figures.blurb: Soviet leader whose openness and restructuring reforms ended the Cold War and led to the largely peaceful breakup of the USSR in 1991.

influenceNote.lenin: Framed perestroika as a return to Lenin's ideas

figures.name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
figures.blurb: As a 1970s lawyer she won Supreme Court cases striking down laws that treated women and men unequally, then served 27 years as a justice.

figures.name: Yuri Gagarin
figures.blurb: First human in space on April 12, 1961, proving people could survive spaceflight and spurring the US race to the Moon.

figures.name: Carl Sagan
figures.blurb: Astronomer whose Cosmos series taught millions about our place in the universe and who helped design the Voyager Golden Records.

figures.name: Elvis Presley
figures.blurb: The King of Rock and Roll, whose fusion of Black and white musical traditions launched a global youth culture.

figures.name: Muhammad Ali
figures.blurb: Heavyweight boxing champion who refused the Vietnam draft on principle, becoming a global symbol of conviction.

influenceNote.malcolm_x: Mentor who guided him into the Nation of Islam

figures.name: Donald Trump
figures.blurb: Businessman and TV personality elected US president in 2016 and again in 2024, whose populist politics reshaped the Republican Party.

influenceNote.ronald_reagan: Revived Reagan's 1980 campaign slogan Let's Make America Great Again

figures.name: Vladimir Putin
figures.blurb: Leader of Russia since 1999 who centralized power and launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, reshaping European security.

influenceNote.peter_the_great: Openly admires Peter; in 2022 likened his war in Ukraine to Peter's conquests

figures.name: Oprah Winfrey
figures.blurb: Talk show host and media entrepreneur whose influence on reading, health and self-improvement reached tens of millions.

figures.name: Angela Merkel
figures.blurb: Physicist turned chancellor who led Germany for 16 years through the euro and refugee crises, anchoring the European Union.

figures.name: Tim Berners-Lee
figures.blurb: Invented the World Wide Web in 1989 and gave it away free, connecting billions of people to shared information.

figures.name: Steve Jobs
figures.blurb: Co-founded Apple and led the Macintosh, iPod and iPhone, putting powerful computers into billions of pockets.

figures.name: Bill Gates
figures.blurb: Co-founded Microsoft, whose software ran most personal computers, then funded global health campaigns against polio and malaria.

figures.name: Barack Obama
figures.blurb: First African American US president, who led recovery from the 2008 financial crisis and expanded health coverage through the Affordable Care Act.

influenceNote.abraham_lincoln: Launched his campaign in Lincoln's Springfield; took the oath on his Bible
influenceNote.martin_luther_king_jr: Took his second oath on King's Bible; heir of the movement King led

figures.name: Jennifer Doudna
figures.blurb: Co-developed CRISPR gene editing with Emmanuelle Charpentier, letting scientists rewrite DNA precisely; they won the 2020 Nobel Prize.

figures.name: Elon Musk
figures.blurb: Led SpaceX's reusable rockets and Tesla's electric cars, speeding the commercial space race and the shift to electric vehicles.

figures.name: Serena Williams
figures.blurb: Won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, the most by any woman in the Open Era, redefining power and dominance in women's sport.
